findings.issue: The inline client script re-implements humanize, filtering, pagination-link building and the Pokémon card that already exist server-side, and the two copies have already drifted (client re-render drops the server's page-status/previous-page/next-page ids).
findings.suggestion: Extract pure helpers (humanize, filter, paginate, buildQuery) into src/lib/pokedex.ts and import them from both the frontmatter and the bundled <script>; Astro client scripts support module imports.

findings.issue: Pure formatting helpers live in the same module as process.env base-URL resolution and the fetch cache, which is why the client duplicates them — a leaky server/client boundary.
findings.suggestion: Split into src/lib/format.ts (pure, importable client-side) and src/lib/server/pokeapi.ts (fetch + cache), keeping the API surface the pages already use.

findings.issue: A Pokémon page request fans out unbounded parallel fetches (all version groups plus every move in the selected game) with no error isolation, and non-404 failures bubble up to an unstyled framework 500 page.
findings.suggestion: Add src/pages/500.astro for a branded error page, and either tolerate individual move failures (render a dash) or bound concurrency of the fan-out.

findings.issue: set:html={JSON.stringify(payload)} does not escape '<', so a '</script>' sequence in API data would break out of the JSON script block.
The full species list (~1,025 entries with absolute sprite/API URLs) is serialised into every home-page response, and the client then re-renders the identical list the server just produced.
findings.suggestion: Skip the client re-render when the parsed state matches the server-rendered page, and consider trimming per-card sprite URLs from the payload.

findings.issue: Byte-identical duplicate of 404.astro; in server output Astro already renders 404.astro for unmatched routes, so one of the two files is dead.
findings.suggestion: Delete the catch-all and keep 404.astro (or vice versa), so future maintainers only update one.

findings.issue: export const prerender = false is repeated in all eight pages although output:'server' already makes it the default (docs annotate it "Not needed in 'server' mode").
findings.suggestion: Drop the exports, or keep exactly one comment noting the app is fully on-demand.

findings.issue: strict:false combined with pervasive any for API payloads means typos in field names (e.g. move.damage_class) fail silently at request time.
findings.suggestion: Enable strict and define interfaces for the API responses the pages actually read (the lib already has good interfaces for MoveDetailRow etc. to build on).

findings.issue: One hardcoded color (#edf0f3) in .moves-table td instead of a design token, unlike every other color in the file.
findings.suggestion: Add or reuse a --color-border token for the row divider.

findings.issue: Unused `children` const (dead code) beside the actual recursive template.
findings.suggestion: Delete it; the recursion is otherwise a clean use of <Astro.self>.

summary: A competent, current-stable Astro 7 SSR app: correct adapter/routing/404 usage per the v7 docs, sensible components and clean CSS. Its one real liability is the server-coupled god data module in src/lib/pokeapi.ts, which forces the home page to duplicate filter, card and pagination logic in an inline client script that has already drifted from the server markup. I'd merge after one round: split the module, share the helpers, add error isolation and delete the redundant catch-all and prerender exports.
